strings.name: Kip Thorne
strings.summary: Born in Logan, Utah, Thorne studied at Caltech and Princeton and researched general relativity, black holes and gravitational waves. He helped establish LIGO’s scientific program, connecting theory with large detectors; the first direct detection was an international team achievement. He shared the 2017 Nobel Prize in Physics with Weiss and Barish. He also coauthored Gravitation, wrote popular science and advised Interstellar.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through November 13, 2026; reviewed November 15, 2026. This is not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Advanced research in relativity, black holes and gravitational-wave theory, contributing to gravitational-wave detection collaborations and science communication.

strings.highlights.h1.title: Gravitational waves and LIGO
strings.highlights.h1.text: Helped establish the detection program and study source theory, building scientific foundations for direct observation.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Communicating relativity
strings.highlights.h2.text: Introduced black holes and spacetime to diverse audiences through textbooks, popular science and film.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Commencement address
strings.timeline.t1.text: Discussed scholarly exploration, breadth of vision and cautious optimism at Caltech’s graduation.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Sharing the Nobel Prize in Physics
strings.timeline.t2.text: Recognized with Rainer Weiss and Barry Barish for key contributions to LIGO and gravitational-wave observation.
strings.timeline.t3.title: LIGO announces direct detection
strings.timeline.t3.text: The international team announced a binary-black-hole signal recorded in 2015.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Science in film
strings.timeline.t4.text: Advised Interstellar and published an accompanying popular-science book.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Helping establish LIGO
strings.timeline.t5.text: Worked with Weiss, Ronald Drever and others on laser-interferometer gravitational-wave collaboration.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Coauthoring Gravitation
strings.timeline.t6.text: Published the general relativity textbook with Charles Misner and John Wheeler.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Caltech faculty appointment
strings.timeline.t7.text: Became associate professor after a research fellowship, continuing relativity and astrophysics.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Princeton doctorate
strings.timeline.t8.text: Completed doctoral physics training, then returned to Caltech for research.
